evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; 字形; 說文; 金文; 廣韻
evidence.text: The entry presents 紹 as 糸 semantic plus 召 phonetic, with primary gloss ‘continue/inherit’ and a later ‘introduce’ sense. It records bronze forms using 幺 or 糸 with 召, sometimes 卩, used as surnames or personal names; the entry does not date those forms. It quotes 說文’s 繼也 and alternate 緊糾也 gloss, and records 綤 as an old form written with 邵. It cites 尚書·盤庚上 紹復先王之大業 and 漢書·敘傳下 漢紹堯運; these support inheritance use in transmitted texts but do not establish when the wording originated. It records 市沼切 and Middle Chinese 常開三宵上.
evidence.kind: specialist dictionary entry and historical-form analysis
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「紹」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Great Xu version of 說文 as ‘紹，繼也。从糸，召聲。一曰紹，緊糾也’; it reports a differing Duan commentary version that reads 古文紹，从卪 rather than 从邵. The entry also lists the uses ‘continue/inherit,’ ‘recommend/introduce,’ and ‘wind around,’ with examples respectively from 書·盤庚上, 戰國策·趙策三 and 晏子春秋, and 樂府詩集. It separately gives a chāo reading glossed ‘slow’; this is a distinct reading and should not be folded into the shào word history. This source documents competing textual readings of the old-form component, not an independently established change sequence.
evidence.title: [A03106] 紹 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Dictionary
evidence.text: Under 紹 shào, the dictionary lists ‘continue/inherit’ and cites 書經·盤庚上 紹復先王之大業; it also lists ‘recommend from the middle’/introduce and cites 戰國策·趙策三 勝請為紹介而見之於將軍 and 晏子春秋. These are dictionary attestations in received works, not independently dated manuscript witnesses.
evidence.title: 紹 : ㄕㄠˋ - 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》

evidence.source: 漢字ペディア (Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation)
evidence.field: なりたち; meanings and readings
evidence.text: The entry describes 紹 as 形声, with 糸 and sound-sign 召 (セウ), proposing ‘joining threads’ as a semantic bridge to ‘succeed’; it reports extensions ‘help’ and ‘mediate/introduce.’ Modern Japanese readings listed are on ショウ and kun つぐ. This is a dictionary’s semantic explanation, not direct proof that the earliest word sense was literally joining thread.
evidence.title: 紹 | 漢字一字

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang 字形演變資料庫
evidence.text: The database describes its selected forms as sourced from Xiaoxuetang’s character databases and ordered oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, then small-seal; its overview says the historical forms and explanations are selected to reflect graphic development. Entry-specific 紹 results were not retrievable in this web session, so this general documentation does not establish any specific 紹 glyph form.
evidence.title: 小學堂字形演變資料庫簡介

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang 字形演變資料庫

The notice grants no basis here to reuse other database content or images from other Academia Sinica sites. No entry-specific 紹 image URL was obtained, so no image is proposed.

evidence.field: 召 rows; lookup for 紹
evidence.text: The local table contains two 召 records: shào with Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[d]awʔ and zhào with *[d]raw-s. The lookup produced no 紹 row. These are distinct readings of 召 and neither is an Old Chinese reconstruction for 紹. The table does not resolve the dossier’s Zhengzhang readings; no Baxter–Sagart sound comparison for the compound host 紹 can be asserted from the available row.
evidence.title: Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction (Baxter and Sagart, 2014)

evidence.text: The transmitted passage reads 紹復先王之大業, an attestation in the ‘resume/carry on the former kings’ enterprise’ sense. The web text is received text and does not establish the wording’s composition date or earliest occurrence.
evidence.title: Shang Shu: 盤庚

evidence.source: 中华人民共和国教育部
evidence.field: 《通用规范汉字表》的基本内容和特点
evidence.text: The Ministry explains that the standard-character table and its appendix present correspondences between standardized characters and traditional or variant forms. It does not provide a character-specific 紹/绍 record on this page. The specialist CUHK entry directly displays 绍 as the simplified counterpart of 紹; this supports classifying the entry-form relation as simplified_form, while exact official form-table evidence was not checked here.
evidence.title: 《通用规范汉字表》的基本内容和特点

search_audit.outcome: Inspected official Xiaoxuetang CC0 notice, Taiwan MOE dictionary entry, and PRC MOE standardization explanation. No exact external direct glyph image was verified. Search results surface transmitted classical examples but do not date textual composition or prove first attestation.

gaps: No usable historical glyph image is proposed: exact Xiaoxuetang 紹 results could not be retrieved, and no exact Commons File description page with original image link was verified. The CC0 notice alone is not an image asset or a form record.

The CUHK entry reports bronze forms, but the specific artifacts, dates, and image sequence were not independently established in this search. The absence of a displayed oracle-bone form is not proof that no oracle-bone form exists.

The earliest secure attestation date for the graph/word and chronology between name use, inheritance, and introduction are unresolved. Received-text dictionary citations are attestations, not proof of composition dates.

The semantic link between literal thread joining and inheritance is a dictionary explanation; primary evidence establishing the metaphorical transition was not found. The Shuowen alternative gloss 緊糾也 is preserved, but its relation to the inheritance sense remains unclear.

Textual accounts differ on the component in the old-form gloss: CUHK and Great Xu text report 綤 from 邵; the Taiwan Ministry page also records a Duan commentary reading 卪. The graphic relationship requires source-specific interpretation and is not resolved here.
The local kMandarin rows say both forms are shào, but official Unicode character pages were inaccessible, so external official click-through verification is absent.

The local Baxter–Sagart table contains two 召 readings and no 紹 row. No valid same-system reconstruction comparison of the host 紹 with a selected 召 reading was established; current Mandarin similarity alone cannot verify ancient phonetic fit.

The official simplification correspondence source was inspected at a general policy level, while the CUHK entry directly marks 绍 as the simplified counterpart. A character-specific PRC standard-table row was not inspected.

limitations.text: No candidate image met the requirement for a verified exact historical-form image URL and provenance page in this run. Xiaoxuetang pages document a CC0 reuse grant for queried glyph images, but the 紹 query failed to return its record and image URLs; no Commons description page for a confirmed 紹 glyph image was found. This is a sourcing limitation, not evidence that suitable images do not exist.
